text:
[LCST.4.5.2] **Defined conversions.** The compiler must classify each defined
`(source, target)` pair total or fallible per this table:

| source → target | class | note |
|---|---|---|
| `Int → Float` | total | widening |
| `Float → Int` | total | a value whose truncation toward zero is an `Int` ([LEXP.7.13.1]): that `Int`. **Any other — non-finite (±Inf, or a NaN an expression computed, [LEXP.4.2]), or finite and outside `Int` — → hard runtime trap** like an `Int` `÷0` ([LERR.1.4.10]). No `?`; see [LCST.4.5.4]. |
| numeric `↔` `Bool` | rejected | no implicit truthiness; use an explicit comparison |
| unit `→` its storage kind | total | `Float` for a `float64` dimension, `Int` for an `int64` or `int32` one ([LUNI.8.7.3]). Strip dimension tag; runtime identity ([LUNI.8.5]); static dim → none ([LUNI.8.7.2]) |
| storage kind `→ <unit>` | total | `Float → <float64 unit>`, `Int → <int64 or int32 unit>`. Assert dimension tag; tag-only, does **not** apply the affine factor ([LUNI.8.5]); result carries the unit's dimension ([LUNI.8.7.1]). A negative `Int` to a `time` unit gives `0_s` ([LTIM.1.3.1]) |
| unit `↔` the other numeric kind | rejected | convert the number first (`x::Int::byte`); falls to [LCST.4.5.3] |
| `Int/Float/Bool → String` | total | `Float` = the canonical `[LDET.3.2.7]` form; see [LCST.4.5.6] |
| `String → Time/Date/Duration` | **rejected** | no temporal text is read ([LTIM.14]); falls to [LCST.4.5.3] |
| `Time/Date/Duration → String` | total | the canonical text form; see [LCST.4.5.9] |
| `Duration → Int` | total | its nanoseconds. `(a - b)::Int - (b - a)::Int` is the signed difference of two instants ([LTIM.1.3.1]) |
| `Duration ↔ <time unit>` | total | one type ([LTIM.1.3.5]); runtime identity |
| `String → Int/Float/Bool` | fallible | parse — requires `::T?`; accepted inputs per [LCST.4.5.7] (`Int`), [LCST.4.5.8] (`Float`), [LCST.4.5.5] (`Bool`) |
| `Bytes ↔ String` | **rejected** | no conversion in either direction; `DS_VALIDATE_BYTES_CONVERSION_RETIRED` ([LSTR.4.6]) |
| any fact-typed `→ Json` | **rejected** | deferred ([LCST.4.5.10]); the compiler must refuse it with `DS_VALIDATE_RULE_NOT_LOWERED` ([RLOW.1.6]) |
| scalar `→ Json` | **rejected** | `Json` is fact-only — falls to [LCST.4.5.3] |
| `Json → scalar` | **rejected** | `Json` is fact-only; read via path projection |
| opaque `→` any non-opaque | rejected | sealed ([LOPQ.4.3]) — the compiler must reject |

idris.name: lcst_4_3_1__fallible
idris.note: The table's classes over the pairs the model carries: the parses `String -> Int`, `String -> Float` and `String -> Bool` are fallible, every other pair total.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_2__convert
idris.note: Int -> Float the widening to the nearest double, Float -> Int the truncation toward zero inside Int and the trap outside it, the identities, the fallible parses String -> Int ([LCST.4.5.7]), String -> Float ([LCST.4.5.8]) and String -> Bool ([LCST.4.5.5]), a value or `null`, and the total renders Int -> String, Float -> String ([LDET.3.2.7]'s canonical form) and Bool -> String ([LCST.4.5.6]). Numeric <-> Bool, the unit rows, the temporal rows and Json are outside the fragment: a trap in the model, refused by the lowering or rejected by the compiler.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_2__guarded
idris.note: Float -> Int with the range test decided: the truncation inside Int, the trap outside it.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_2__in_int
idris.note: -2^63 <= x < 2^63 on exact doubles, built from the Int as formal/k/dscast.k builds them; a NaN fails both comparisons and an infinity one.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_2__int_to_float_is_total
idris.note: The widening row for every Int.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_2__trunc
idris.note: Toward zero over the primitive cast with dscast.k's one-step correction, right whichever way the primitive rounds; run on dscast.k's vectors in Main.idr, not proved against the primitive, which is why it is partial.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_4__float_to_int_is_total
idris.note: The Float -> Int row for every Float: that Int inside the range, the trap outside it, never null.
